gaps.sentence: Our team ___ the championship twice in the last five years.
gaps.hint: in the last five years up to now
gaps.explanation: 'In the last five years' is a period up to the present, so the present perfect fits: has won.

gaps.sentence: This month they ___ a new wing to the hospital, so some services are elsewhere.
gaps.hint: this month means a temporary current period
gaps.explanation: 'This month' describes a temporary situation around now, so the present continuous fits: are adding.

gaps.sentence: Jane ___ her phone at home, and it drives me mad.
gaps.hint: annoying habit shown with always continuous
gaps.explanation: 'Always' with the present continuous expresses an irritating habit: is always leaving.

gaps.sentence: By the time you read this letter, I ___ the country.
gaps.explanation: An action completed before a future point takes the future perfect: will have left.

gaps.sentence: I ___ here for two years, so I know the system well.
gaps.hint: for two years continuing until now
gaps.explanation: 'For two years' with present relevance takes the present perfect, often continuous: have been working.

gaps.sentence: I ___ dinner when the lights went out.
gaps.hint: the lights went out interrupted it
gaps.explanation: The lights going out interrupted an ongoing background action, so the past continuous is used: was cooking.

gaps.sentence: The company ___ its profits every year since it changed strategy, and analysts expect more growth.
gaps.hint: since clause anchors past to present
gaps.explanation: A 'since' clause connecting a past start to the present requires the present perfect: has increased.

gaps.sentence: They ___ so much since they started the new school.
gaps.hint: since they started with present result
gaps.explanation: Change measured from a past starting point to now takes the present perfect: have grown.
